courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Infectious Diseases and Their Control
courses.description: The course aims to help students to understand clinical infectious diseases and their control. Emphasis will be placed on clinical and nursing aspects including principles of diagnosis and treatment, epidemiology and prevention strategies, methods of surveillance, development of policies on infection control and the clinical impact of infection control teams in the hospital and community.
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Understand common community-acquired and hospital-acquired infectious diseases, and their management and control

2. Understand strategies and methods for epidemiological surveillance

3. Identify statutory procedures for notification of infectious diseases

4. Describe strategies for outbreak management

5. Apply the concepts of prevention and management of hospital-acquired infections

6. Understand the roles and responsibilities and occupational risks of health care providers and infection control teams in health care settings

7. Critically evaluate various strategies and policies on infection control

8. Discuss preventive measures against infectious diseases and the related protection and control policies
courses.course_syllabus:
Understanding Infectious Diseases and their control

- Microbiology and pathogens leading to Infectious Diseases

- Epidemiology and surveillance

- Basic concepts of infection control, standard and transmission-based precautions, isolation precaution

Common Infectious Diseases and their management

- Common Infectious Diseases related to respiratory, gastrointestinal systems, skin, tropical infectious diseases, HIV, SARS, Avian Flu and their management

- Common healthcare associated infections and their management

Preventive measures, protection and control policies

- Preventive measures against spread of infection including personal, environmental, food etc

- Disinfection and sterilization

- Immunization and vaccinations

- Infection control policies and statutory notification procedures

- Roles and responsibilities of infection control team

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Culture and Nursing
courses.description: This course aims to facilitate students' understanding of the theories and concepts about culture that are relevant to nursing and enable them to provide person-centred care in a multicultural healthcare context.
courses.learning_outcomes:
By the end of the course the students will be able to:

1. Examine the relationship between culture, society, and nursing practice.
2. Apply cultural theories and their basic inquiry skills to study health beliefs andpractices.
3. Discuss the influence of Chinese culture on the practice of nursing.
4. Analyse theories and concepts underpinning the delivery of transcultural nursing.
5. Examine the role of nurse in providing person-centred care in a multicultural healthcare context.
6. Develop the ability to conduct cultural assessment.
7. Apply principles of transcultural nursing to provide culturally specific and congruent nursing care to clients of different cultures.
courses.course_syllabus:
* *Health in different cultures:**

Chinese, South Asian, Japanese, Australian, French, and Korean conceptions and practices on health

* *Cultural implications on health:**

Cultural implications on body and beauty, food and health, life and death, illness prevention

* *Transcultural nursing:**

Trends of transcultural nursing studies, culture and social conflict, ethno nursing inquiry skills, Leininger’s theory of culture care and diversity and universality, Giga and Davidhizar’s transcultural assessment model, cultural sensitive communication skills and techniques

* *Psychology of culture and health:**

Cultural diversity, demography
courses.feedback_evaluation:
The course adopts a number of formal and informal measures to generate feedback for evaluation about the course. Students are encouraged to use the CU eLearning System and email to post your views, and class representatives are invited to collate the views of students during and at the end of the course. Another means of evaluation is using Course and Teaching Evaluation to evaluate the course. There are also opportunities for students to feedback about the course, lectures, tutorials and lab days during the staff-student consultative committee. During the lectures, tutorials and lab days, students are welcomed to approach the teaching staff to give their feedback as well.

Students can review their assessment materials. The review period will be held within two weeks after grades are released to students. The date will be determined by the Course Coordinator. Student who wishes to review the assessment materials must make a formal request to the Year Administrator within four calendar days after grades are released.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Application of Public Health and Epidemiology in Nursing
courses.description: This course aims to develop students' ability to understand the principles and theories of public health and epidemiology. Emphasis will be on the application of these principles and theories in nursing practice to promote population health.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: The Hong Kong Health Care System
courses.description: The aims of this course are to develop students' ability to understand and analyse the health care system in Hong Kong, with emphasis on structures, policies, and contemporary issues underpinning the provision of health care. Shifts in the organisation of health care provision and their implications for nursing practice will be examined.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Scholarly Inquiries in Nursing
courses.description: This course provides students the opportunity to design a scholarly inquiry or project such as concept analysis, literature review or a proposal on a specific nursing or health-related problem. Students will select a topic of interest to them under the supervision of a faculty member. Through the learning process, students will deepen knowledge and techniques in scholarly project and nursing research.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of the course, the students should be able to

1. Demonstrate knowledge and skills in critically evaluating nursing and healthcare research.

2. Design a scholarly inquiry project on a specific nursing or healthcare-related problem.

3. Apply evidence-based knowledge to inform nursing practice.

4. Demonstrate innovation and creativity with the ability to think critically from multiple angles.

5. Demonstrate ability in writing a scholarly inquiry project proposal.
courses.course_syllabus:
1. Conducting literature search

2. Critical appraisal skills

3. Quantitative research methodology

4. Qualitative research methodology

5. Project planning and evaluation

6. Design a scholarly inquiry project proposal
courses.feedback_evaluation: Students are welcome to give feedback at any time throughout the semester via both formal and informal mechanisms which are adopted to generate feedback for evaluation. Students are encouraged to post their views on the Blackboard Learn discussion forum or approach the course coordinator or teachers to give their feedback. Class representatives are invited to collect views from fellow students and express their comments and concerns for consideration and discussion at the staff-student consultative committee meeting. At the end of the semester, students will be invited to anonymously fill in the ACCESS evaluation forms to make comments and suggestions about the course and the teaching performance.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Scholarly Inquiry I
courses.description: This course aims to help students develop knowledge and skills to critically appraise literature resources with a focus on advanced nursing practice. This will involve analyzing the contribution of research and appropriateness of the research approaches to knowledge development.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Nursing
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, students will be able to:
1. Analyze the processes for establishing current evidence for specific areas of nursing practice.
2. Identify the benefits and limitations of evidence-based practice.
3. Critically review the literature that underlies a selected healthcare topic.
4. Evaluate the designs and methods commonly used in research and service innovation project.
5. Discuss quality of measurement in both quantitative and qualitative research.
6. Develop a critical review of the literature in a selected area of a nursing topic.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Advanced Health Assessment and Clinical Judgment
courses.description: This course provides students with opportunities to apply their knowledge and skills of comprehensive history taking and physical assessment to both healthcare and community settings, with emphasis on differentiation between normal and abnormal findings, identification of common health problems, process of critical thinking and clinical judgment through analysis of clinical findings.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Nursing or Doctor of Nursing
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, students will be able to:
1. Perform and document comprehensive health history and physical assessments in a selected area of health care.
2. Compare and contrast the principles and techniques in advanced health assessment including physical, psychological, socio-cultural, family and community assessments.
3. Apply a model of assessment appropriate to the student's discipline.
4. Accurately analyze health assessment data and identify clinical problems.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Evidence-based Practice for Quality Care
courses.description: This course facilitates students to expand their scope of clinical practice by undertaking an in-depth examination of their specialty area of practice. Students are expected to further develop their skills in clinical decision-making and to promote evidence-based practice in their relevant clinical specialty.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Nursing or Doctor of Nursing
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, students will be able to:
1. State the development of evidence-based practice in nursing and its implications for advancing nursing knowledge and practice.
2. Describe and clarify the major roles of advanced practice nurses/ nurse consultants in the planning and implementation of advanced nursing practice.
3. Analyze critically the existing nursing practice specific to their specialty area, and compare and contrast with the best empirical evidence.
4. Apply the clinical problem-solving skills to analyze how to improve quality of care.
5. Design an innovative and scientific based intervention in their practice area to support advanced nursing practice.

courses.description: This course focuses on developing students' understanding of healthcare management, leadership and the process of health outcome evaluation. Related frameworks for healthcare management, continuous quality improvement and outcome evaluations will be explored to guide students in assuming a managerial role and making quality improvement decisions in their specialty practice.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Nursing or Doctor of Nursing
courses.learning_outcomes:

1. Examine organizational, leadership and change theories which will help students develop clinical leadership, assume a managerial role in healthcare management, and manage changes in clinical practice.
2. Explore and critique methods for evaluating healthcare interventions and outcomes.
3. Critically apply the contribution of process and outcome evaluation in the planning of continuous quality improvement project in healthcare organization.

In addition, reflection of the process of literature review and the strategies used to overcome difficulties during the development of the scholarly inquiry project will be shared and discussed.

courses.learning_outcomes:

1. Describe and justify the literature and research methods selected to inform the development of their scholarly inquiry project.
2. Use appropriate strategies to search the literature relevant to their project.
3. Critically analyze the research methods and the literature related to their own project or the projects presented by their peers.
4. Discuss significant issues related to their own and their peers’ review of the literature.
5. Discuss and reflect the process of literature review and the strategies used to overcome difficulties during the development of the scholarly inquiry project.
6. Present their scholarly inquiry project in a clear and logical manner.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Advanced Biostatistics in Evidence-based Practice Research
courses.description: The aim of this elective course is to provide students with an advanced level of knowledge in biostatistics and to enable them to appropriately apply such knowledge for evaluating nursing innovation in the complex health care context. This course also enables the students to have an advanced level of statistical literacy to appraise the science in nursing and health care.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Doctor of Nursing
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, students will be able to:
1. Develop the knowledge and skills to read, critically evaluate, and discuss the advanced biostatistics in scientific nursing literature.
2. Develop the knowledge and skills in conducting a variety of statistical techniques for calculating the sample size in evaluating an evidence-based nursing practice.
3. Critically discuss the methods and considerations in identifying an appropriate statistical method for evaluating an evidence-based nursing practice.
4. Develop the knowledge and skills in conducting a variety of statistical techniques for evaluating the effects of an evidence-based nursing practice.

3. Demonstrate critical thinking skills in integrating the analysis and synthesis of the evidence-based nursing knowledge into their writing.
4. Disseminate significant components of the research/ service innovation project for knowledge development and transfer.
5. Utilize the research findings to meet the changing healthcare needs and to enhance the quality of care.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Clinical and Translational Research in Nursing
courses.description: This course is offered in Term 1 to pair up with NURS7114 as a year-long course. The course aims to equip students with knowledge on theoretical, methodological and statistical concepts for the development, implementation and evaluation of clinical and translational research in nursing. Emphasis is placed on the processes of critical appraisal, analysis and integration of research evidence, developing clinical questions for scientific inquiry, obtaining and appraising best evidence, and applying the evidence to inform professional development of clinical nursing.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Doctor of Nursing
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, students will be able to:
1. Critically discuss the role of nursing knowledge and science in clinical and translational research in nursing.
2. Critically integrate nursing knowledge and science to inform the development of a research topic and the methodology for the research.
3. Critically discuss the principles, applications, strengths, and limitations of various research designs and sampling methods in clinical and translational research in nursing.
4. Critically discuss the principles, applications, strengths and limitations of various data collection methods in clinical and translational research in nursing.
5. Describe a range of data analysis techniques for analyzing qualitative and quantitative data, and discuss their applications in clinical and translational research in nursing.
6. Describe the purposes and methods of systematic review and discuss its application in clinical and translational research in nursing.
7. Identify a topic area for the evidence-based research project and critically discuss its significance to inform advanced nursing practice and nursing education.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Research Seminar
courses.description: This course is offered in Term 1 each study year to pair up with NURS7124 as a year-long course. The course aims at enabling students to develop skills in scholarly presentation and discussions and enhance their critical thinking abilities in planning, implementing, evaluating and applying evidence-based nursing innovations. The seminar also facilitates sharing of research ideas and methodological issues between doctoral students and academic staff, contributing to the development of the students’ evidence-based practice Research Projects.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Doctor of Nursing
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, students will be able to:
1. Critically discuss their own and others’ research problems and the significance of their research to the professional development in nursing.
2. Understand the applications of different research methodologies as scientific tools to address various clinical and professional issues in nursing.
3. Critically discuss and evaluate the methodological issues arising from research presentations.
4. Disseminate their research proposals and findings effectively, and demonstrate the techniques to justify all the decisions involved in the study design, interpretation of results and discussions.
5. Engage constructively in the scholarly discussion of research presentations.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Innovation in Advanced Nursing Practice: Theory, Application and Evaluation
courses.description: The aim of this course is to enable students to explore and critically analyse the process of developing, implementing and evaluating innovations in advanced nursing practice. The course consists of three major components: 1) providing students with opportunities to critically examine the epistemological debates about nursing science, and the influences of classical and contemporary nursing theories in shaping the innovative development of advanced nursing practice; 2) explore and critically discuss the innovative models of advanced nursing practice and the contemporary issues in the application of such models across the continuum of care; and 3) critically discuss the strategies and methods for identifying nurse sensitive outcomes in the evaluation of the effects and cost of advanced nursing practice.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Doctor of Nursing or MPhil-PhD in Nursing
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, students will be able to:
1. Critically appraise and evaluate the concepts, classical and contemporary theories, and science underpinning the discipline of nursing and the corresponding contributions to the development of innovative nursing practice models.
2. Critically discuss the process of translating and integrating scientific evidence and nursing knowledge to inform advanced nursing practice.
3. Critically analyse, evaluate and apply the knowledge and theory underpinning clinical decision-making to achieve clinical excellence in nursing services.
4. Critically analyse and evaluate the contemporary legal and ethical issues in relation to the development and implementation of innovative nursing practice.
5. Critically discuss the concepts, knowledge and framework for evaluating the effectiveness of innovative nursing practice in meeting complex health care needs.
6. Critically discuss the criteria and considerations for identifying nursing sensitive outcomes in the evaluation of innovative nursing practice.
7. Critically discuss the concepts, methods and contemporary issues relating to cost-effective analysis for evaluating innovative nursing practice.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Clinical Practicum
courses.description: The aim of this clinical practicum is to prepare students for active roles and develop their competences in nursing leadership, advanced clinical decision making and evidence-based nursing innovations for managing the complex health care environment. Students will be provided with an intensive overseas clinical shadowing experience in high quality health care organizations. They will also be provided with opportunities and guidance in using reflective approach to optimize their learning outcomes through clinical exposure. By the end of this course, they will be able to conduct a critical discussion on how the advanced model in nursing service provision can be applied to the health care systems in their own countries.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Doctor of Nursing
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, students will be able to:
1. Critically evaluate the integration of theory and practice in clinical setting.
2. Analyse and evaluate different approaches and models of nursing leadership, clinical decision making and advanced nursing practice in clinical setting.
3. Critically reflect, analyse, reconsider and examine their own clinical experiences relating to nursing leadership, clinical decision making and advance nursing practice.
4. Critically evaluate the health care outcomes in relation to different approaches in nursing leadership, clinical decision making and advanced nursing practice.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Research Project Supervision
courses.description: This course is offered in Term 2 of Year 2 to provide students with individual evidence-based practice research supervision. The students are coached to critically apply the knowledge generated from their clinical and translational research to develop an evaluation protocol. This protocol will be used to evaluate the effectiveness of the nursing innovation developed in NURS 8112 at individual, organizational and/ or community levels. The students are required to obtain ethical approval for conducting scientific evaluation of the nursing innovation.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Doctor of Nursing
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, students will be able to:
1. Critically discuss the research designs appropriate for evaluating the clinical effectiveness of the nursing innovation developed in NURS8112 in relation to nurse sensitive outcomes.
2. Critically discuss the methods of sampling appropriate for evaluating the clinical effectiveness of the nursing innovation developed in NURS8112 in relation to nurse sensitive outcomes.
3. Critically discuss the data collection methods appropriate for evaluating the clinical effectiveness of the nursing innovation developed in NURS8112 in relation to nurse sensitive outcomes.
4. Critically discuss the data analysis methods appropriate for evaluating the clinical effectiveness of the nursing innovation developed in NURS8112 in relation to nurse sensitive outcomes.
5. Critically discuss the rigour of the research methodology proposed to evaluate the clinical effectiveness of the nursing innovation developed in NURS8112 in relation to nurses sensitive outcomes
6. Critically appraise the finalized evaluation protocol for nursing innovation prior to submission for ethical approval.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Research Project Supervision
courses.description: This course is offered in Term 2 of Year 3 to provide students with individual evidence-based practice research supervision in client sampling, implementation of nursing innovation, process monitoring, and data collection. The students are provided with opportunities to critically integrate their knowledge into clinical and translational research, clinical leadership and decision making, as well as advanced nursing practice to facilitate successful implementation of the nursing innovation. This course enables students to consolidate the knowledge that they have learnt in the previous study years and translate such knowledge to real practice.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Doctor of Nursing
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, students will be able to:
1. Demonstrate appropriate techniques to accurately implement the innovative nursing protocol.
2. Demonstrate appropriate techniques to monitor the integrity of the innovative nursing protocol and response promptly and appropriately to undesirable adverse events.
3. Demonstrate appropriate techniques to collect research data and to maximize data validity and reliability.
4. Demonstrate appropriate techniques to monitor and record any factors which may influence the evaluative outcomes of the innovative nursing protocol.
5. Demonstrate appropriate techniques to manage research data.
6. Demonstrate appropriate techniques to respond appropriately to barriers which hinder evaluative data collection.
7. Demonstrate appropriate techniques to ensure that ethical principles and guidelines are strictly followed in the implementation of nursing innovation.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Research Project Supervision
courses.description: This course is offered in Term 1 of Year 4 to pair up with NURS8104 as a year-long course. The course provides students with individual evidence-based practice research supervision in the process of analysing the data collected for evaluating the nursing innovation and reviewing the process of its implementation. The students are provided with opportunities to interpret the study findings, critically discuss the implications of the findings on advanced nursing practice, nursing professional development and nursing science advancement. The course also enables students to discuss a systematic plan on how to translate the developed evidence to immediate nursing practice.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Doctor of Nursing
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, students will be able to:
1. Apply appropriate methods to conduct qualitative and quantitative data analysis for evaluating the evidence-based innovative nursing protocol.
2. Present evaluative data in an orderly, logical, systematic, and accurate manner.
3. Accurately interpret research data and make relevant and appropriate conclusions on clinical effectiveness and applicability of the evidence-based innovative nursing protocol.
4. Critically discuss and integrate research findings in the context of existing nursing knowledge and explain similarities and differences.
5. Critically consider the limitations of the study and their associated impacts on research findings.
6. Critically discuss the clinical implications of the research findings for nursing practice, nursing theory and/ or nursing research.
7. Demonstrate the academic skills in writing up a thesis which entails sufficient amount of details to permit a thorough critique of the overall research study.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Research Project Supervision
courses.description: This 5-unit course is offered in Term 2 of Year 4 to pair up with NURS8103 as a year-long course. The course provides students with individual evidence-based practice research supervision in the process of analysing the data collected for evaluating the nursing innovation and reviewing the process of its implementation. The students are provided with opportunities to critically discuss the implications of the evaluative findings on advanced nursing practice, nursing professional development and nursing science advancement. The course also enables the students to discuss a systematic plan on how to translate the developed evidence to immediate nursing practice. By the end of this course, the students are required to integrate theoretical and clinical knowledge in their empirical research study and submitting a thesis for assessment prior to graduation.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Doctor of Nursing
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, students will be able to:
1. Apply appropriate qualitative or quantitative methods to conduct data analysis for evaluating the evidence based innovative nursing protocol.
2. Present the evaluative data in an orderly, logical, systematic, and accurate manner.
3. Critically interpret evaluative data to examine clinical effectiveness of the evidence-based innovative nursing protocol.
4. Critically consider the alternative explanations of the findings and present scientific rationale for their rejection.
5. Critically consider the limitations of the study and their associated impacts on research findings.
6. Critically discuss the clinical implications of the research findings for nursing practice, nursing theory and/ or nursing research.
7. Demonstrate the academic skills in writing up a thesis which entails sufficient amount of details to permit a thorough critique of the overall research study.

courses.title: Group Research Project Supervision
courses.description: This course is offered in Term 1 of Year 2 and Year 3 to provide students with interactive workshops and tutorials to strengthen their knowledge on research methodology, facilitating them to critically apply such knowledge to their research project in a nursing specialty.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Doctor of Nursing
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, students will be able to:
1. Critically discuss the research methodology in developing nursing science.
2. Critically discuss the application of relevant research methodology in the nursing research project.
3. Critically discuss the pros and cons of the research design being used in the nursing research project.
4. Critically discuss the strategies used to monitor the quality of an ongoing nursing research project.
